findings.issue: HIG is the only family whose wrapper is built with no norm-statistics policy: `HIGWrapper(model, ctx.loss_fn_svd, device)` gets no `bn_mode`, and `HIGWrapper.output_and_loss_grad` (experiments/optimizers/hig.py:121-141) runs TWO train-mode forwards per step through `functional_call` (the `jacrev` forward and the plain `self._forward` for `y_pred`), neither suppressed. Measured on `SmallResNet` (float64): the jacrev forward changes 18 of 27 buffers, the second forward changes 18 more, and `num_batches_tracked` stays `[0,0,0]` because the in-place `add_` goes to the reparametrised copy while `F.batch_norm`'s stat update reaches the real buffers. End to end through `run_grid` on SmallResNet, an 8-step run gives HIG `num_batches_tracked=[0]`, `max|running_mean|=0.5012`, while svd (gram full, gram chunked and classic), SGD, LBFGS(max_iter=3) and JD all give `num_batches_tracked=[8]` = exactly one update per optimizer step (`max|rm|` 0.3501/0.3501/0.3501/0.3521/0.3519/0.4143). So HIG's running statistics advance at twice every other optimizer's rate (effective momentum ~0.19 vs 0.1) and its eval-mode val/test numbers are measured under a different normalisation than every method it is compared against — a re-occurrence of F2/F3, the defect C-E2 exists to remove. The checkpointed state_dict is also internally inconsistent (running_mean moved, count 0), which breaks `momentum=None` semantics and C-L4 offline replay for any HIG run on a norm-stat model. Exposure: campaign/plan_campaign.yaml:344-347 (`p3_cifar_jd_hig`, currently `enabled: false`) plus any HIG override on resnet/finetune configs; nothing in the code or the tests would stop it.
findings.suggested_fix: Give HIGWrapper the SvenWrapper treatment: wrap the jacrev and the `y_pred` forward in `no_norm_stat_updates(self.model)`, add one explicit `torch.no_grad()` train-mode `self.model(x)` per step (skipped when `norm_stat_modules(self.model)` is empty), accept `bn_mode`, and pass `bn_mode=bn_mode` at generic_scan.py:868 (hig.py belongs to another track — report it). Stop-gap in a file the integrator owns: in `execute`, after `model.load_state_dict`, `if spec.family == 'hig' and bn_mode == 'batch' and norm_stat_modules(_ckpt_module(model)): raise ValueError(...)` so the run becomes a loud `error` record instead of a plausible-looking number.

findings.issue: `default_bn_mode` makes the effective BatchNorm policy PER FAMILY (`frozen` for svd+gram, `batch` for everything else) whenever a config names neither `bn_mode` nor `gram_freeze_norm_stats`. CONTRACTS.md "Config keys" specifies `bn_mode: batch` as the scan-level default and C-E2's goal is literally "One BatchNorm policy for every optimizer". Under the per-family default a Gram scan on a BN model trains Sven with frozen statistics and its baselines with batch statistics, with no run_id marker on either side (`bn_mode_suffix` emits nothing because each family matches its own default) and only the line `bn_mode per-family default` in the job header. Every CIFAR config in the tree happens to set one of the two keys today, so no current scan is affected — but a new gram config, or a `+use_gram=true` / `mode=svd` override on a BN model, silently reproduces F2/F3.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the per-family rule for the run_id only (`bn_mode_suffix` is right), and close the silent case in `execute`: after the model exists, if `ctx.settings['bn_mode'] is None` and `norm_stat_modules(_ckpt_module(model))` is non-empty, raise with "this model has norm layers; set bn_mode: batch|frozen explicitly". ~4 lines, leaves every norm-free config (MNIST/toy/poly/nanoGPT, where frozen vs batch is a no-op) byte-identical, and makes a mismatched scan impossible rather than merely unlikely.

findings.issue: C-E2's acceptance test is specified for "Sven (`full` and `chunked` capture) and for LBFGS with `max_iter=3`", but `test_one_step_updates_running_mean_exactly_once` / `test_frozen_mode_never_changes_a_buffer` are parametrised over SGD and LBFGS only, both through `train_loop_standard`. Nothing anywhere asserts the BN contract for the svd family, HIG or JD, and the loops track explicitly handed "BatchNorm + Sven" to integration (campaign/stage0_reports/loops.impl.md, "Left to integration"). `tests/test_runner_training.py::test_bn_mode_reaches_the_record_and_the_run_id` only checks the record field and the run_id suffix. I verified the svd and JD paths by hand and they are correct; the same 20-line check would have caught the HIG defect above.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one test to tests/test_runner_training.py that drives `run_grid` on `experiments.nn.nets.SmallResNet` with `bn_mode: batch` and a 4-family grid (svd gram full, svd gram chunked, SGD, LBFGS, jd, hig) and asserts, from each run's final checkpoint, `{int(v) for k,v in state.items() if k.endswith('num_batches_tracked')} == {n_train//batch_size*num_epochs}`; plus a `bn_mode: frozen` variant asserting every buffer is bit-identical to the init state.

findings.issue: `run_hash` hashes the raw `rcfg['dataset']` and `rcfg['model']` containers. Any cosmetic edit to a dataset/model yaml while a scan is in flight — spelling out a value that was already the default (`n_test: 10000`), renaming a key, reordering a nested block that json canonicalisation does not normalise away — changes `hash8` for every run of that scan, and `run_grid` then MOVES every jsonl/npz/ckpt into `_stale/{old_hash8}/` and re-executes the lot. The eval settings were deliberately hashed *resolved* (`_HASH_EVAL_KEYS`, docstring: "otherwise a config tidy-up would re-execute the whole campaign") for exactly this reason; the two biggest hash inputs were not given the same protection. With a 5-day deadline and the configs track still editing yamls, this is live.
findings.suggested_fix: Either hash a normalised projection of the two configs (`_target_` plus sorted scalar leaves, with `None`-valued keys dropped so adding an explicit default is a no-op), or — cheapest — state in CONTRACTS.md "Stage 1" that a scan's `dataset`/`model` yaml is frozen once its first job is submitted, and add a `--hash-diff` mode to tools/reconcile.py that prints old-vs-new hash8 per run and refuses to relaunch without `--yes` when more than 10% of finished runs would be retired.

findings.issue: `grid.hash8(spec, rcfg)` is computed from the composed config, but `run_grid` (generic_scan.py:1151-1158) mutates `cfg.model`/`rcfg['model']` with the dataset's `vocab_size` (and `block_size`) before hashing, because `experiments/configs/model/nanogpt.yaml` deliberately omits `vocab_size`. reconcile therefore computes a different hash8 from the runner for every LM scan, so a complete `exp_nanogpt_speedrun` (a P0 item, 5 seeds x 4 lrs x 6 baseline lrs) reports every finished run as `stale-hash`, i.e. "work remains". No results are lost (a relaunch re-derives the injected hash and skips), but the status the launch decisions are made from is wrong and the queue slots are wasted. Part B's report notes this; nothing in the tree fixes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the injection into a function in grid.py (which the integrator owns), e.g. `grid.inject_dataset_facts(rcfg, vocab_size=None, block_size=None)`, call it from `run_grid` and export the facts so reconcile can apply the same mutation without importing torch — or have reconcile read `{scan}/configs/{job}.yaml` (already written by `_save_resolved_config`, post-mutation) in preference to composing the live config.

findings.issue: `oom` and `error` are retried by the dedup rules, with no attempt cap. A DETERMINISTIC error — `EpochPermutationSampler` raising `no full batch of B in N examples` for `batch_size > n_train`, `Muon`'s new `no hidden weight matrix` raise, a bad `_target_`, a missing token `test.bin` — therefore produces an `error` record and a `done/{run_id}.{h8}.error` marker, and every subsequent worker and every resubmission re-executes it and rewrites both. Over a 5-day campaign with hundreds of jobs a single config typo is re-attempted hundreds of times, and nothing in `run_grid`'s Counter or the console output distinguishes "failed once" from "failing forever".
findings.suggested_fix: `_stale_hashes_now` already globs `done/{run_id}.*`; reuse that listing to count this hash's `error`/`oom` markers and skip the run (counting it as `poisoned`) above a threshold (3), or — if the retry must stay unconditional — make tools/reconcile.py print a `permanently failing` section listing run_ids with >=2 error markers at the current hash so the operator sees it on the first status pass.

findings.issue: Part A's report claims "Run-id neutrality proved: scratch script compared HEAD's grid.py with mine over HEAD's configs — 264 (config, mode) pairs, 0 differ". That is not reproducible: comparing `git show HEAD:experiments/experiment_code/grid.py` against the working tree over all 46 configs x 6 modes gives 255 identical, 21 DIFFERING. All 21 are the CIFAR/finetune configs: every `cifar10_resnet_*`, `profile_cifar` and `rebuttal_fig5_cifar_paramfrac_scan` svd run_id gains `_gram_bnbatch`, and every non-svd `exp_finetune_cifar_smallN` run_id gains `_bnfrozen`. Both changes are CORRECT — `tests/golden/cifar10_resnet_scan_labelRegression.txt` contains 90 real on-disk run_ids ending `_gram_bnbatch`, and HEAD's grid.py (line 255, `rcfg.get('gram_freeze_norm_stats', True)`) did not understand the new `bn_mode: batch` key and so silently dropped the legacy suffix; `tests/test_grid.py:544` and `:274` pin the new behaviour. The defect is the verification claim, not the code: as written it tells the orchestrator that no run_id moved relative to HEAD, when in fact every CIFAR Sven run_id and every finetune baseline run_id did.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the report: state that 21 of 276 (config, mode) pairs differ from HEAD, that the differences are exactly the restored `_gram_bnbatch` and the new `_bnfrozen` tokens, and that the oracle is the golden file rather than HEAD's grid.py (HEAD's grid.py + the committed configs was the broken combination). Also note in the report that `stop_on_nonfinite` ended up `True` (grid.py:368), contradicting Part A's deviation 2.

findings.issue: `train_eval_size` is unset, so it defaults to 10,000 while the Shakespeare train split is ~7k blocks; `_ScanContext._train_eval_dataset` then returns `train_dataset` itself (`n_eval >= n_train`), and every epoch end evaluates val (~868) + test (~868) + the WHOLE training set (~7k blocks) — about 8.7k forward passes against ~7k training steps, 50 times per run, on the one scan whose headline claim is wall-clock ("Report val loss vs steps AND wall-time"). The same shape applies to MNIST (10k val + 10k test + 10k train_eval = 30k eval examples per epoch against 50k training examples) and CIFAR (5k + 10k + 10k = 25k against 45k). Part A flagged the nanoGPT case but with the arithmetic an order of magnitude off ("10,000 blocks ~10M tokens"; it is ~7k blocks, ~0.9M tokens).
findings.suggested_fix: Set `train_eval_size: 1000` in exp_nanogpt_speedrun.yaml and `2000` in the MNIST/CIFAR headline configs — `train_eval` is a fixed-subset estimator of the training loss, not a quantity that needs the full split, and the subset is already split-seed-derived and shared by every optimizer so the comparison stays paired. (configs track owns the yamls.)

findings.issue: The diff contains more than the `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath` line the integrator's brief allows: the `dev` dependency group gains `nbconvert>=7.17.1` (with a `uv.lock` change alongside it). Whoever made it, the branch that `tools/deploy_snapshot.sh` exports now carries an uncommitted lock bump.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm ownership (the analysis track's `make_plots.sh` is the stated reason) before the orchestrator commits, and keep the lock change in its own commit so a snapshot's `DEPLOY_INFO.json` sha maps to a known environment.

findings.issue: `_train_eval_dataset`'s docstring claims "`subsample_indices` returns a prefix of one permutation, so the subset is also nested in `n_train`". It is not: the call is `subsample_indices(n_train, n_eval, split_seed)`, which permutes `range(len(train_dataset))`, and `train_dataset` itself changes size with `n_data`. For `rebuttal_overparam_mnist_scan` (n_data 2500..50000, `train_eval_size` 10000) the n_data=20000 and n_data=40000 runs therefore measure `train_eval` on different example sets, so the `train_eval` curve is not comparable across P/N points. The invariant that matters — one fixed subset for every optimizer within a scan — does hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the nesting claim from the docstring and note in the analysis conventions that `train_eval` is comparable within a scan only, or make it true by drawing the subset from the POOL indices (`dataset.train_indices` where available) instead of from positions inside the already-subsampled `train_dataset`.

findings.issue: `_ScanContext`'s comment (generic_scan.py:511-518) says the loops "reduce with .mean(), which is the identical gradient" when handed `SVD_LOSS_FNS` instead of `STANDARD_LOSS_FNS`. That is true for `ce`, `label_regression`, `brier` and `lm_ce`, but false for `mse` on a multi-output target: `SVD_LOSS_FNS['mse']` sums over the output dimension before the batch mean, so `_scalar_loss(...)` is D x `nn.MSELoss()` and the effective learning rate of every first-order baseline is scaled by D. Every campaign config that uses `mse` has a scalar output (D=1), so nothing is wrong today — but the comment invites a future multi-output regression config that would silently compare baselines at a D-fold different lr.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the comment to "identical gradient for every loss key in this campaign, because the only `mse` targets are scalar; a multi-output `mse` config would scale the first-order lr by the output dimension", or assert `ypred.shape[-1] == 1` for `loss == 'mse'` in `resolve_scan_settings`/`execute`.
